# `•index` — Fresh indices

`•index n` gives `⍳n` along an axis with a fresh name. `stem •index n` starts the name with the text `stem`. The name is `_`, the stem, `·` and a random part of 64 bits written as 13 digits, as in `_b·k3f9q2m7x1c0p`. Two calls give different names, except with a chance of about one in 10¹⁹. `•index` maps over an array of numbers, with the same stem for each. It also maps over a nested array: one call can make every index that a formula needs. A keyed shape gives a record of indices with the shape's keys. Plain `•index⍴x`, with no stem, is the usual form:

```bpl
x←2 3⍴⍳6 ⋄ [[n i] h]←•index[⍴x 4]
⍴:x.[n i]×h                ⍝ [2 3 4]ₓ
k←["n":2 "i":3]⍴⍳6
•index⍴k                   ⍝ ["n":[0 1]ₓ "i":[0 1 2]ₓ]
```

A name that starts with `_` is hidden. Plain display leaves hidden axis names out. Any key or name that starts with `_` and contains `·` displays up to its last `·`, then `…`. Box mode, `⍴` and error messages show a fresh name as `_b·…`. To keep a long key or name of your own short on screen, start it with `_` and put a `·` before the part to leave out: `["_note·long description":3]` displays as `["_note·…":3]`. `•literal⁻¹` writes every name in full. A hidden name meets a visible one as if that axis had no name, and the result keeps the visible name:

```bpl
i←•index 3 ⋄ v←⍳["v":3]
i          ⍝ 0 1 2
⍴i         ⍝ ["_·…":3]ₓ
⍴i+v       ⍝ ["v":3]ₓ
```

Indices with different names build a grid, in arithmetic and in selection. An index used twice pairs with itself. Here `x.[i]-x.[j]` holds the difference between every pair of items of `x`, and `m.[i i]` is the diagonal of `m`:

```bpl
x←10 20 40 ⋄ [i j]←•index 3 3
⌈/,|x.[i]-x.[j]      ⍝ 30
m←[1 2 3⋄4 5 6⋄7 8 9]
+/m.[i i]            ⍝ 15
```

Indices name the axes of a formula, as einsum's letters do. In this product, [`+.×⍠k`](../glyphs/dot.qmd) sums along `k`, the index that both operands share. `b` and `o` build the result's grid. [`⍉⁻¹`](../glyphs/circle-backslash.qmd) reorders its axes by name:

```bpl
xu←[2 3]⍴⍳6ₓ ⋄ wu←[3 4]⍴⍳12ₓ
[b o k]←•index 2 4 3
y←xu.[b k]+.×⍠k⁝wu.[k o]
∧/,y=xu+.×wu                 ⍝ $t
∧/, [o b]⍉⁻¹y = ⍉xu+.×wu     ⍝ $t
```

[Models in index notation](../index-notation.qmd) builds a neural network and a transformer's attention with indices.

Names from `•index` can't collide with the names on a caller's data. [`⍳["i":n]`](../glyphs/iota.qmd) gives a name that the caller chooses.

[`∂`](../glyphs/partial.qmd) of a dfn that uses `•index` runs from a program, as `∂` of any other dfn does. Each call's result still has new names. A map calls such a dfn once on all its cells, as [Evaluation](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects) describes for any dfn. The cells share each name that the dfn draws. Where the dfn's result holds one of those names, the map calls the dfn once for each cell instead. Each cell's result then has names of its own.

Errors: `DOMAIN` for a stem that isn't text.
